completion:
Begin with the section of your report dedicated to the methodology. This section should include a detailed explanation of how the study was conducted. Describe the procedures, participants, materials, and any measures or scales used. In case of contradictions, this information will be crucial for readers to understand the context in which the results were obtained.

3. Provide the hypothesis.
Re-state the original hypothesis clearly and concisely. This sets the stage for the discussion of contradicting results and helps readers remember what was initially expected from the study.

4. Present the data analysis.
Explain how you analyzed the data, including the statistical tests employed. Present the key findings as they emerged from the data. Ensure that your analysis is transparent and replicable. Include tables, figures, or charts to make the data more understandable.
